learningObjectives: Explain the importance and benefits of mobile test automation.
Install and configure Tosca Mobile and TMA for testing readiness.
Explore local and cloud-based connection options in Tosca Mobile.
Capture and interact with mobile app elements using scanning options.
Execute reliable and scalable mobile tests using Tosca Mobile.

elements.term: A deep dive, not a single lesson
elements.description: AE1's 'Automating beyond web applications' course touches Mobile Engine 3.0 in a single lesson — enough to open a Mobile Scan and build one TestCase. This course goes much deeper: installing and configuring TMA yourself, preparing both Android and iOS targets, understanding Local vs Remote topologies, scanning native/hybrid/web mobile apps, and working through the full catalog of mobile-specific Modules and gestures.

elements.term: One engine, three kinds of app
elements.description: Mobile Engine 3.0 automates native apps (built specifically for iOS/Android), hybrid apps (a native shell wrapping embedded web views, common in cross-platform frameworks like React Native or Ionic), and mobile web (a site opened in the device's browser). The same Mobile Scan handles all three — the difference shows up in how controls are captured, not in a different tool.

elements.text: This is a Deep Dive course and part of the Tricentis Tosca On-Prem Product Consultant learning plan — the same learning plan as AS1/AS2, TDS1/TDS2, and AE1. It assumes the AS1/AS2 fundamentals (Modules, TestCases, TestStepValues, ActionModes) are already comfortable.

bulletPoints: AE1 = one Mobile Engine lesson as part of a broader 'beyond the browser' course. This course = a full deep dive into mobile alone.
Native, hybrid, and mobile web are all reached through the same Mobile Scan and the same Mobile Engine 3.0.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: What you will be able to do

elements.title: Course objectives, lesson by lesson
items: Mobile Engine 3.0 & TMA — understand the architecture: what runs where, and why TMA removes the need to hand-configure Appium.
Installing and configuring TMA — get the agent running on Windows and macOS, locally and headless.
Preparing Android — USB debugging, drivers, emulators via Android Studio, and the APK-signing gotchas that trip up training material.
Preparing iOS — Xcode, Developer Mode, simulators vs physical devices, and why iOS automation needs a Mac.
Connecting Tosca to TMA — test configuration parameters (TCPs), Local vs Remote topologies, and the most common connection mistake in the whole course.
Mobile Scan — capturing native, hybrid, and web mobile controls, including hybrid webview context switching.
Building your first mobile TestCase — the mandatory Open Mobile App step, gestures, and text entry.
Advanced Modules & troubleshooting — hardware buttons, orientation, biometrics, file transfer, session lifecycle, and a systematic way to diagnose failures.

bulletPoints: The course builds in one direction: environment → connection → scanning → authoring → the wider Module catalog.

elements.text: Official course description: this course covers how Tricentis Tosca Mobile and the Tricentis Mobile Agent transform mobile test automation by streamlining processes and boosting test coverage — installing Tosca Mobile, configuring its architecture, and using its scanning and execution options for reliable, scalable mobile testing.

elements.title: Recommended prior training
items: Tricentis Tosca Fundamentals — Automating web application testing (AS1).

elements.title: Technical prerequisites
items: Access to Tricentis Tosca, including a valid licence for Tosca Mobile — a training licence can be requested from the Tricentis Support Hub.
Access to the Tricentis Mobile Agent (a separate installer from Tosca Commander itself).
Android Studio downloaded and set up — needed for the Android emulator used across the course's device-prep and scanning lessons.
At least one Android target: a physical device with USB debugging enabled, or an emulator created through Android Studio.
Optionally, at least one iOS target: a physical device or the iOS Simulator — both require a Mac, since Xcode only runs on macOS.

elements.text: iOS automation cannot run from a Windows machine. If Tosca Commander itself runs on Windows, iOS testing needs a separate Mac running TMA, connected to the Windows machine as a Remote (TMA) setup — covered in the Connecting Tosca to TMA lesson.

bulletPoints: Official prerequisites, grouped: Knowledge (testing + mobile automation basics) · Training (AS1 recommended) · Technical (Tosca Mobile licence, TMA access, Android Studio).
Android-only learners can complete the whole course on Windows or macOS.
iOS work requires a Mac somewhere in the topology, even if Tosca Commander stays on Windows.

elements.description: Roughly half of this course is environment setup — installing TMA, preparing devices, wiring the connection — before a single Module gets scanned. That ordering matches reality: the large majority of 'mobile automation isn't working' problems in practice are setup and connection problems, not TestCase-authoring problems.

elements.text: Every lesson pairs explanation with concrete, checkable steps (install commands, settings paths, TCP values) rather than abstract theory alone — mobile setup is where small details (a missing trailing slash, a disabled toggle) cause the most confusing failures.

bulletPoints: Expect setup-heavy early lessons and authoring-heavy later lessons.
Small configuration details are called out deliberately — they are also where most real-world mobile automation problems hide.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing this course with AE1's Mobile Engine lesson
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming everything already covered by AE1's single mobile lesson is all there is to know.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: This course covers TMA installation, both mobile platforms' device prep, connection topologies, and the full mobile Module catalog in depth — material AE1's single lesson only introduces.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to automate iOS from a Windows-only setup
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Installing TMA on Windows and expecting to scan an iOS app or simulator.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: iOS automation always needs a Mac running Xcode somewhere in the picture — either as the machine running Tosca and TMA together, or as a Remote (TMA) machine that a Windows Tosca Commander connects to.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does this course differ from AE1's Mobile Engine lesson?

options.text: It uses a different automation engine entirely.
It is a full deep dive into mobile setup, connection, scanning, and the wider Module catalog, where AE1 covers only the basics in one lesson.
It only covers mobile web testing, not native apps.
It replaces the need for a Tosca licence.

practiceQuiz.hint: Same engine (Mobile Engine 3.0), much more depth.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Both courses use Mobile Engine 3.0. AE1 gives one lesson's worth of coverage; this course dedicates full lessons to TMA installation, Android and iOS device prep, connection topologies, and the broader Module catalog.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A learner's Tosca Commander runs on a Windows machine with no Mac available anywhere. What mobile automation can they still perform?

options.text: Neither Android nor iOS — a Mac is required for all mobile automation.
Android automation, using a physical device or an Android Studio emulator.
iOS automation only, via the iOS Simulator on Windows.
Both platforms equally, since TMA abstracts away the OS difference.

practiceQuiz.hint: Xcode — and therefore the iOS Simulator and iOS device automation — only runs on macOS.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Android automation works fine from Windows with a physical device or an Android Studio emulator. iOS automation always requires a Mac somewhere in the topology, since the tooling Mobile Engine 3.0 relies on for iOS is Xcode-based and Xcode is macOS-only.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why does this course spend roughly half its lessons on environment setup before any TestCase authoring?

options.text: Because Mobile Engine 3.0 requires more TestSteps than other engines.
Because in practice most mobile automation failures come from setup and connection issues, not authoring mistakes.
Because setup lessons count double toward the Final Exam.
Setup is optional and can be skipped by experienced learners.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about where confusing failures actually originate in mobile testing.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The course deliberately front-loads environment and connection setup because that is where the large majority of real-world 'mobile automation isn't working' problems originate — not in TestCase design itself.

Same engine, far more depth. AE1 gives one introductory lesson; this course is a dedicated multi-lesson course.
Native, hybrid, and mobile web — all through the same Mobile Scan.
Tosca licence with Mobile Engine 3.0 · install rights for TMA · at least one Android target; iOS optional but needs a Mac.
iOS automation always requires a Mac (Xcode) somewhere in the topology, even with Tosca Commander on Windows.
Setup-heavy first half (TMA, devices, connection) → authoring-heavy second half (scanning, TestCases, advanced Modules).
